item.text: {"decisions":[{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0001","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0001 is the document header containing navigation elements, CIDOB institutional boilerplate, and basic biographical identifiers (name, dates, party, political affiliation). No policy content, legislative agenda, budget priorities, appointments, fiscal rules, regulatory quality, anti-corruption enforcement, infrastructure delivery, information reliability, tax-incidence, shock response, or economic trajectory assessment appears.","exclusion_reason":"Navigation header and basic biographical identity block; contains no policy content relevant to any 5B question."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0002 covers López Obrador's 2018 electoral victory framing, campaign discourse, historical vote share (53.2%), and political positioning. It describes rhetorical style and electoral success but contains no specifics about legislative agenda, budget allocation, professional appointments, fiscal rules, competition policy, anti-corruption enforcement, infrastructure quality, economic information reliability, distributional incidence, shock response, or inherited vs outgoing economic trajectory.","exclusion_reason":"Political narrative framing and electoral history; no policy substance relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0003 covers the 2006 electoral dispute, claims of fraud (0.56% margin), civil disobedience campaign, and the 'Coalition for the Good of All.' The content concerns electoral legitimacy and opposition tactics, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral dispute narrative; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Unit-0004 documents López Obrador's opposition to Peña Nieto's structural reforms — energy, education, labor, and telecommunications — characterizing them as corrupt, weak, and contrary to national sovereignty. This constitutes evidence on whether the ruler's legislative agenda pursued broad-based prosperity vs rents (5B.1), whether fiscal/tax/energy rules protected stability (5B.3), whether competition and regulatory frameworks were fair (5B.4), and whether anti-corruption enforcement was applied to politically connected actors (5B.5).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Unit-0005 presents the 2018 campaign platform's economic program in detail: 'austeridad republicana' redirecting public resources from current spending to investment without tax increases; social causes including poverty and human development for vulnerable groups; energy self-sufficiency via domestic gasoline production; food self-sufficiency with guaranteed prices for local producers; eradication of political corruption 'giving example' from the presidency; and migration defense. This directly addresses 5B.1 (prosperity agenda vs rents/loyalty), 5B.2 (appointments/professional processes), 5B.3 (fiscal/macroeconomic rules), 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement), 5B.6 (budget quality/infrastructure), 5B.7 (reliable economic information), 5B.8 (distributional fairness), and 5B.9 (shock response).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Unit-0006 describes López Obrador's platform as 'pragmatic social democracy' that accepts orthodox free-market principles, macroeconomic stability, budget discipline, and peso floatation while rejecting privatization and prioritizing national production. It also records his promise to fight corruption and privilege without vengeance ('no voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel'). This speaks to 5B.1 (legislative agenda orientation), 5B.3 (macroeconomic rules credibility), 5B.4 (competition/property rules), 5B.5 (anti-corruption against politically connected actors), 5B.6 (budget quality), and 5B.8 (distributional policy).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0007 covers migration caravans, the USMCA trade deal, and border tensions with Trump. While trade policy has some economic relevance, this chunk focuses on migration politics and diplomatic friction rather than domestic economic governance, rule quality, budget execution, anti-corruption enforcement, or economic trajectory assessment.","exclusion_reason":"Migration diplomacy and USMCA mention; no substantive domestic economic governance content for any 5B question."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0008 covers López Obrador's childhood, family background, early influences (Benito Juárez, Marxist philosophy), 1969 family tragedy, and relocation to Palenque, Chiapas. Pure biographical material with no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Early biography and personal history; no policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0009 covers López Obrador's university enrollment at UNAM (1972), political baptism via 1976 campaign for Carlos Pellicer, introduction to Tabasco governor Leandro Rovirosa Wade, and PRI functionary positions (INI delegation, Secretary of Promotion). No economic policy content relevant to 5B.","exclusion_reason":"University enrollment and early PRI career; no policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0010 covers López Obrador's COPLAMAR delegation (1978), indigenous publications and agricultural programs, UNAM teaching, marriage to Rocío Beltrán Medina, and three children. Personal and early administrative career; no economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Administrative career and family life; no policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0011 covers PRI committee work in Tabasco (1983), conflicts with party leadership, 1984 relocation to DF (INCO), 1986 publication on Tabasco history, 1987 UNAM degree, and joining the Democratic Current within PRI. No specific economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Party internal conflicts and early political formation; no economic policy substance for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0012 covers the 1988 elections, formation of the Democratic National Front (FDN), Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas presidential run, López Obrador's Villahermosa gubernatorial candidacy, and fraud allegations. Electoral history; no specific economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"1988 electoral fraud allegations; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0013 covers PRD founding (May 5, 1989), López Obrador as Tabasco PRD president, the 1991-1992 'exodus for democracy' march, electoral fraud complaints, and 1992 settlement recognizing PRD victories in Cárdenas and Nacajuca municipalities. Electoral and party-formation history; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"PRD founding and democratic march; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0014 covers the 1994 Tabasco gubernatorial election (lost to Roberto Madrazo with 38.7%), fraud allegations, 1995 'caravan for democracy' march, creation of the National Democratic Alliance, and opposition to Salinas's Pemex segmentation. Electoral dispute narrative; economic elements are incidental to the fraud/protest framing.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral protest and opposition tactics; no substantive economic governance policy assessment for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0015 covers PRD electoral failures under Muñoz Ledo's leadership, López Obrador's election as PRD president (July 1996, 73.9% vote), and his leftist positioning within the party. Party internal politics; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"PRD internal politics and party leadership election; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0016 covers PRD electoral successes (1997-1999) including Cárdenas's DF government election, PRD legislative gains, state governorships (Zacatecas, Tlaxcala, Baja California Sur), and PRD internal election chaos culminating in Jesús Ortega's presidency. Party electoral and internal history; no economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"PRD electoral victories and internal disputes; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0017 covers Cárdenas's resignation from DF government (September 1999), López Obrador's emergence as successor, and his FOBAPROA research/book ('Fobaproa, expediente abierto') denouncing the 1994 banking bailout as unconstitutional and 'the biggest fraud since the Conquest.' While FOBAPROA has economic dimensions, this unit focuses on López Obrador's opposition narrative and personal research career, not on his own economic governance agenda as a ruler. The content does not assess his own legislative agenda, appointment quality, fiscal rules, competition policy, anti-corruption enforcement, budget quality, information reliability, distributional incidence, shock response, or economic trajectory — it is a critique of a prior administration's policy.","exclusion_reason":"FOBAPROA critique of prior administration (Salinas/Zedillo); does not describe López Obrador's own economic governance agenda or performance as ruler."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0017","unit-0019"],"explanation":"Unit-0018 covers López Obrador's 1999 PRD primary victory (75.5%) and 2000 federal election victory in DF (34.5%, defeating PAN's Santiago Creel and PRI's Jesús Silva Herzog). It establishes his accession to DF government with a coalition including PT, Convergencia, PAS, PSN, and PCD. Relevant as context for his subsequent DF governance record (unit-0019 onward) which included social programs and infrastructure.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"Unit-0019 covers López Obrador's DF government (2000-2005): intense public works campaign for urban infrastructure improvement and expansion; social protection programs including the Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores (Universal Food Pension for Seniors); resistance to implementing the Seguro Popular; and evaluations of his performance as voluntary, committed to social welfare, austere (simple apartment, utilitarian car), and focused on accountability and transparency. This bears on 5B.1 (broad-based prosperity vs patronage), 5B.2 (appointment approach), 5B.6 (budget quality and infrastructure delivery), and 5B.8 (distributional incidence across social programs).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0020 covers López Obrador's personal reputation (Peje, AMLO nicknames), communication style (mañaneras press conferences), and image as either a hardworking, socially committed leader or an extremist/populist lacking professional qualifications. Character assessments and media strategy; no specific economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Character reputation and media style; no substantive policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0021 covers mixed evaluations of López Obrador's DF government: vigorous public works vs accusations of populist budget spending and growing debts; crime-fighting results received disparate assessments. While infrastructure spending is mentioned, this unit is primarily evaluation of his management rather than specific policy details needed for 5B assessment. No specifics on appointment quality, fiscal rules, competition policy, anti-corruption enforcement, information reliability, distributional mechanisms, shock response, or trajectory assessment.","exclusion_reason":"Mixed evaluations of DF government management without specific policy details needed for 5B assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0022 covers the March 2004 video scandal: Televisa broadcast of clandestine recordings showing PRD officials (Gustavo Ponce, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz) involved in corruption (casino gambling, money negotiation with Argentine businessman Carlos Ahumada). Explains origins of the scandal, the individuals involved, and Ahumada's extradition. Corruption facts present but from the video scandal period (2004) rather than López Obrador's presidential term, and the content is narrative/explanatory rather than assessing his anti-corruption enforcement record as president.","exclusion_reason":"Video scandal narrative; corruption facts relate to DF subordinates in 2004, not López Obrador's own presidential anti-corruption enforcement under 5B.5."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0023 covers the political fallout of the video scandal: PRD break with implicated officials, corruption charges, Rosario Robles's forced departure, and López Obrador's late/timid reaction. He attributed the scandal to a 'conspiracy' by former president Salinas, Fernando Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox administration. This describes his response to corruption within his own circle, but does not contain evidence of his enforcement of anti-corruption rules, cooperation with audits/courts, or remedy of favoritism as required by 5B.5 during his presidency.","exclusion_reason":"Video scandal political fallout; López Obrador's response to subordinates' corruption rather than his own anti-corruption enforcement record as president."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0024 covers the May 2004 desafuero request by the PGR related to a 2000 land expropriation dispute in Cuajimalpa, initiated under Rosario Robles's DF government. The text describes the legal conflict, PRD accusations of political motivation ('inhabilitate him as a candidate in 2006'), and the threat to his political future. Legal dispute narrative; no economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Legal desafuero dispute; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0025 covers the August 2004 demonstration of 200,000 PRD members in support of López Obrador, his October 2004 book 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación,' and Fox's November 2004 dismissal of Marcelo Ebrard as Mexico City Public Security Secretary. Political mobilization and personnel changes; no specific economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Political mobilization and book publication; no substantive economic policy assessment for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0026 covers the April 2005 Chamber of Deputies vote (360-127) approving desafuero, the resulting civil resistance movement with hundreds of thousands protesting in the Zócalo, and López Obrador's legal defense arguments transcribed in his 2005 book. Political confrontation narrative; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero political battle; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0027 covers the PGR's inability to get a judge to initiate proceedings (April 2005), Fox's acceptance of Attorney General Macedo de la Concha's resignation, and López Obrador's return to office. Also covers his July 2005 request for leave from DF government to focus on PRD primary, and Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas's withdrawal from the primary. Resolution of legal/political conflict; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Legal resolution of desafuero; no economic policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0028 covers the 2006 presidential campaign launch in Metlatónoc, Guerrero (the country's poorest municipality), his campaign coalition 'Por el Bien de Todos,' and main adversaries (Felipe Calderón for PAN, Roberto Madrazo for PRI). Campaign launch narrative; no specific economic governance policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Campaign launch; no substantive economic policy details for 5B assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0029 covers Calderón's campaign characterization (FeCal nickname, elite representation), López Obrador's accusations against Calderón regarding BANOBRAS and Energy Ministry nepotism/abuse, and polarization dynamics. Electoral positioning; no substantive economic governance policy assessment.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral polarization and campaign accusations; no specific economic policy content for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0030 covers the PAN's negative campaign spots ('López Obrador es un peligro para México'), the 'Por el Bien de Todos' program framework emphasizing ending privileges, corruption, and 'saqueo' from the federal administration; fraud investigation; and civil service salary reduction as first step. While the program mentions austerity and anti-corruption as policy intentions, this is pre-presidency campaign content and does not constitute evidence of executed budgets, appointment quality, fiscal rules enforcement, competition policy, anti-corruption enforcement, or infrastructure delivery.","exclusion_reason":"Campaign program intentions; insufficient specificity on executed economic governance for 5B assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0031 covers the 2006 PRD economic program: social programs funded by austerity savings (100 billion pesos first year), new fiscal revenue from improved collection, public service extension to degraded areas, elderly/ unemployed/mothers support, productive activities in agriculture/tourism/construction, and Pemex protection from privatization. Campaign program content; describes intentions rather than executed governance and lacks specificity on rule quality, anti-corruption enforcement mechanisms, or distributional implementation.","exclusion_reason":"Pre-presidency campaign program; describes intentions without executed governance evidence for 5B assessment."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0032 covers López Obrador's distancing from Chávez and Venezuela, no personal relationship with Chávez, and PRD's skepticism toward Bolivarian strategy. Foreign policy positioning; no domestic economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Foreign policy and Venezuela relations; no economic governance content for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0033 covers the July 2006 election night and PREP results showing Calderón's 0.64% lead, electoral irregularities claims (50,000 suspicious ballot boxes), and international election observation missions (EU) confirming process integrity. Electoral dispute narrative; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"2006 electoral dispute narrative; no economic governance policy content relevant to 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0034 covers international election monitoring (OEA, EU, UN) confirming process integrity, PRD gains in legislative elections, and López Obrador's July 8 launch of total battle to 'prove' he won, massive Zócalo rallies, and 'peaceful civil resistance' with road blockades. Electoral opposition mobilization; no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral opposition mobilization; no economic governance content for 5B."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0035 covers the TEPJF's partial recount order (August 5), López Obrador's rejection and call for intensified resistance, his August 15 invocation of Article 39 constitutional article, and the August 28 partial recount results confirming the 0.56% margin.
